statement: L05, L06, and L07 do not supply exact quotes for one shared intervention, so the axis comparison is unresolved. L05 describes a composite of terminal-leaf count or boosting-round count with ensemble size under squared loss. L06 describes learner capacity, printed as P leaf or P boost, and ensemble size under squared loss and test MSE. L07 describes split-candidate count, with depth, ensemble size, and the leaf-count bound held fixed in its conclusion, and reports RMSE. L08 is a kernel-ridge analysis under RMSE, symmetric trees, randomization, and shrinkage; it is not a vote that those three interventions are the same.

axis_by_source.L05: Composite and separate sweeps of P leaf or P boost and P ens under squared loss.
axis_by_source.L06: Learner capacity (P leaf or P boost) and ensemble size P ens, composite and single-axis, under squared loss and test MSE.
axis_by_source.L07: Split-candidate count M, with native per-feature border budget B as another control, under RMSE.

unresolved_points: L05 and L06 vary leaf or boosting-round capacity together with ensemble size. L07 varies split-candidate count and its conclusion holds ensemble size fixed.

L05 increases P boost until squared training error is approximately zero and then fixes P boost. L06 fixes P boost = 200 in the quoted third boosting experiment. The extracts do not identify these schedules with each other.

L05 prints the interpolation threshold as p=n and as p = n. L06 defines it as parameter count equal to the number of training samples and marks a dotted line. L07 places a peak near a path-span crossing in M and reports training RMSE already close to zero there, without calling that crossing the interpolation threshold.

The located losses are squared loss and RMSE. CatBoost logloss is absent from L05, L06, and L07. L05 does not name CatBoost, L06 names scikit-learn, and L07 names CatBoost, XGBoost, and LightGBM in the RMSE experiments.

L06 reports that the double-descent pattern disappeared on its single-axis sweeps. L07 reports interior peaks while split-candidate count changes and a monotone random-forest curve on that sweep. The sentences refer to different interventions.

The located samples differ: L05 uses MNIST with ntrain = 10000 in the main text, L06 uses 500 CRyPTIC isolates and 500 Friedman samples, and L07 uses California Housing with ntrain = 1000 unless a panel changes sample size, plus 18 regression datasets.
L07 also varies training checkpoint along M in one figure, and some panels vary depth or sample size. Those panels are not the same held-fixed split-candidate intervention as the conclusion sentence.

L08 assumes RMSE, shrinkage, symmetric oblivious trees, and randomization for a kernel equivalence. It contains no double-descent or interpolation wording and does not establish a common axis for L05, L06, and L07.
